title: CRLR/81/2017 of Rajeev Bhatia Vs Smt. Seema Devi AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Delay Condonation Application No. 514 of 2017
In
Criminal Revision No. 81 of 2017
Rajeev Bhatia Ö..Revisionist
Versus
Smt. Seema Devi Ö.Respondent
Mr. Pankaj Kapil, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Prem Kaushal, Advocate for the respondent.
Dated: 24.07.2017
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
 Heard.
2. Delay Condonation Application, being
unopposed by the respondent, is allowed. Delay in
filing the criminal revision is condoned.

3. This criminal revision has been preferred by
the revisionist against the judgment and order dated
19.11.2016 passed by the learned Judge, Family
Court, Pauri Garhwal in Miscellaneous Criminal Case
No. 54 of 2016 ìSmt. Seema Devi v. Rajeev Bhatiaî
under Section 125 of Cr.P.C., whereby the learned
Judge has allowed the application of respondent under
Section 125 Cr.P.C. and the revisionist is directed to
pay the maintenance to the respondent @ ` 4000/- per
month as well as ` 1000 to his daughter.
4. The matter was placed before the Mediation
Centre of this Court. In the mediation proceeding, the
parties have arrived at following compromise:
ì1. Now there is no dispute between the
parties and both the parties have settled
their dispute amicably and are ready to live
together. Moreover, both of them are living
together.

2
2. It has been settled by the parties that
they will live together and respondent Smt.
Seema Devi shall have no objection if the
Criminal Revision No. 81 of 2017, pending
before this Court is allowed in the light of
compromise and the proceeding of lower
court will be withdrawn by the respondent
Smt. Seema Devi.
3. It is further submitted that Mr. Rajeev
Bhatia (revisionist) will also withdraw the
case pending before the Family Court,
Bijnor, under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage
Act.
4. It is further submitted that both the
parties are ready to be bound by the
conditions of the settlement/compromise.
5. That the parties hereto confirm and
declare that they have voluntarily and out of
their own free will arrived at this
settlement/agreement in the presence of the
mediator.
6. That the settlement has been read over
& explained to the parties in their own
language. Signature of parties are also
identified by their Advocates.
7. That both the parties are bound by the
terms and conditions of this settlement
agreement.î
5. Learned counsel for the parties submitted
that the settlement arrived at by the parties be
recorded. Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted
that the revision be dismissed as not pressed.
6. In view of above stated facts and in view of
the fact that parties are living together, the prayer is
allowed and revision is dismissed as not pressed.
7. All the pending applications also stand
disposed of.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
24.07.2017
Navin
